The PR changes only documentation, per the patch excerpts and changed ranges: head lines 444-448 (drain semantics) and 1974 (handshake deadline row). Security-relevant docs change: a lifecycle drain may complete without coordinator acknowledgement when no work remains and no coordinator session is registered (for example while reconnecting). A registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. This concerns TB-002 and the availability and accounting of in-flight inference. I see no regression in the documentation. The behavior is implemented in unsupplied code (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, ServiceDrain.swift). The next pass should confirm that this fallback cannot be reached while a session is registered or while terminal usage is still unacknowledged, so billing or usage reporting is not lost.

A second row documents a 30 s coordinator handshake deadline (CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.defaultTimeout). A stalled handshake is cancelled and retried with the existing backoff. This is availability hardening touching TB-002 and does not alter the attestation or serving-authorization flows (TB-011, A-016). The implementation is unseen.

The base units I examined describe the add-on hold (TB-012, T-059), the prefix cache (T-041) and the logout and unenroll text. None of it is altered by the head changes, and I found no conflict with the threat model. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the source code is not supplied.
